The 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election took place on 3 May 2012, as part of the wider local elections held across the United Kingdom on that date.

Here are the key details about this election:

**Election Format:**
- One third of the council was up for election (21 seats out of 63)
- Elections were held in 21 of Stockport's 21 wards
- The council operated on a thirds system, with elections in three out of every four years

**Results:**
- The Liberal Democrats lost control of the council, which they had held since 2011
- No party achieved an overall majority, resulting in No Overall Control (NOC)
- The Labour Party made significant gains
- The Liberal Democrats suffered losses, reflecting their national unpopularity at the time as junior coalition partners in the UK government

**Context:**
- This election took place during a difficult period for the Liberal Democrats nationally
- The Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government was implementing austerity measures
- Local elections across England in 2012 generally showed poor results for both coalition parties

**Aftermath:**
- Following the election, Labour became the largest party but without an overall majority
- The council continued under No Overall Control
- This marked a significant shift in Stockport's political landscape

The 2012 election was part of a broader pattern of Liberal Democrat losses in local elections during their time in the coalition government (2010-2015), with many councils they previously controlled moving to either Labour control or No Overall Control.
